summary: Both Scripture quotes are KJV-verbatim and the doctrine/Christ-landing is sound, but the opening line implies the cry of dereliction was Jesus' first utterance from the cross, which contradicts the gospel record.

findings.beat: Beat 1 (hook) — 'From the cross, Jesus did not speak His own words first — He cried a psalm David had written a thousand years before.'
findings.quote_or_claim: From the cross, Jesus did not speak His own words first — He cried a psalm David had written a thousand years before.
findings.problem: The phrase 'did not speak His own words first' reads as a chronological claim that the cry of dereliction (Matt 27:46) was Jesus' opening utterance from the cross. In the harmonized gospel record the dereliction cry is the FOURTH of the seven sayings; 'Father, forgive them' (Luke 23:34) and the word to the penitent thief ('To day shalt thou be with me in paradise', Luke 23:43) precede it. Matthew/Mark record only this cry, so 'first' is not supportable. The intended point is that the cry was borrowed Scripture rather than original speech — fix the wording so it does not assert a false order.
findings.proposed_fix_text: From the cross, Jesus cried words that were not His own — a psalm David had written a thousand years before.
